purpose: First live evidence-module acceptance round: five real NR3D utterances per module; exploratory validation, not a benchmark.
selection: Manual semantic coverage selection before inference from six locally prepared ScanNet validation scenes. All rows have correct_guess=True, at least two stimulus candidates, and valid GT-table IDs. Select supported predicates, ambiguity or missing-evidence boundaries, and combinations; do not inspect predictions or metric agreement. Preserve original utterances, including alias mismatches. All 25 rows are distinct, and all six scenes are excluded from the fixed 300 manifest. This is a module regression and coverage batch, not a held-out accuracy sample.
runtime_input: Original query plus full prepared scene and annotated object table. Never narrow runtime candidates with the stimulus or target ID.
known_regression_note: These rows were already in previous size or scene0011 trial manifests and are retained for semantic regression coverage. Selection did not use previous model outcomes; the other rows may also have been explored before, so no held-out claim is made.

rows.query: choose the smallest table.
rows.acceptance_focus: Execute the size condition over the frozen full-category pool; record measurement reliability and proxy metric before final acceptance.

rows.query: The tallest trashcan.
rows.acceptance_focus: Use vertical height, not volume or point count; retain ties or unreliable measurements as uncertain.

rows.query: The smaller of the cabinets.
rows.acceptance_focus: Preserve the of-the-cabinets comparison scope and distinguish comparative evidence from a bare small adjective.

rows.query: choose the tall skinny shelf
rows.acceptance_focus: Record both tall and skinny; short horizontal side alone cannot certify skinny. Require justified semantics or visual evidence and keep unknown attributes missing.

rows.query: Choose the smaller of the two cabinets that are above the big cabinet. It has a green note attached to it.
rows.acceptance_focus: Bind the big-cabinet reference, freeze the above-reference comparison subset, and separately inspect the green note. Unbound subset or part evidence must block acceptance.

rows.query: the trash can closest to the door
rows.acceptance_focus: Retain each legal door anchor_id and the distance metric; keep near ties or anchor-dependent winners uncertain.

rows.query: This table is the farthest from the door.
rows.acceptance_focus: Compute the farthest ranking on the initial comparison pool and require consistent reference binding.

rows.query: The cabinets closest to the double doors.
rows.acceptance_focus: Bind double-door semantics and preserve separate physical anchors rather than averaging them into a virtual door.

rows.query: The table near the door.
rows.acceptance_focus: Return geometric distance evidence without silently treating near as nearest; an uncalibrated fuzzy predicate remains missing.

rows.query: Of the two rectangular tables (not square), choose the one closest to the door.
rows.acceptance_focus: Bind rectangular and not-square conditions before defining the two-table comparison pool; a global nearest table cannot discharge this query.

rows.query: The picture above the photocopier
rows.acceptance_focus: Bind picture as subject and photocopier as reference; record vertical interval and horizontal alignment with boundary uncertainty.

rows.query: Select the table underneath the TV.
rows.acceptance_focus: Normalize underneath to below consistently in parse recovery, rewrite, audit and executed geometry.

rows.query: The trashcan in between printer and wooden desk
rows.acceptance_focus: Evaluate the target against two distinct bound references and inspect wooden on the desk role. Missing reference appearance cannot be transferred to the trashcan.

rows.query: The table with white chairs under it
rows.acceptance_focus: Resolve it to the target table and check chair below table, equivalently table above chair. White applies to chairs.

rows.query: Wall mounted cabinet, the one that's not above printer
rows.acceptance_focus: Record wall-mounted and negated-above conditions separately. Unsupported negation or support evidence must retain missing rather than accept a positive above winner.

rows.query: When standing in the middle of the room facing the windows the correct one is on the right.
rows.acceptance_focus: Derive the language frame from explicit room-center origin and window-facing information, preserve legal facing hypotheses, and require a common right-side result.

rows.query: When facing the windows, the one on the left.
rows.acceptance_focus: Facing constrains orientation but does not imply room-center standing. An unbound observer origin must remain missing.

rows.query: The left window.
rows.acceptance_focus: Retain the left condition and report missing origin/facing. A convenient rendering camera cannot become the speaker frame.

rows.query: Facing the back of the chairs, the chair on the left.
rows.acceptance_focus: Chair backs need explicit orientation or visual evidence; a point-cloud long axis cannot certify the back or the speaker origin.

rows.query: When standing in the middle of the room facing the carts the correct one is on the far left and is a green and blue color.
rows.acceptance_focus: Apply far-left under one consistent language frame and inspect green and blue independently; camera changes must not change the direction interpretation.

rows.query: choose the blue cart.
rows.acceptance_focus: Inspect blue for every still-possible cart and record visibility, per-candidate verdicts and unknown reasons.

rows.query: choose huge wooden cabinet.
rows.acceptance_focus: Separate wooden material evidence from huge size semantics; one yes must not discharge both attributes without explicit support.

rows.query: brown table next to table with rainbow top
rows.acceptance_focus: Bind brown to the target table and rainbow-top to the reference table, inspect both roles, and keep uncalibrated next-to evidence explicit.

rows.query: You want the table standing against the wall that has different colored stripes on top, maybe painted, with blue, red, yellow, green, and blue, and then again on the bottom shelf.
rows.acceptance_focus: Track each distinct color, stripes, top and bottom-shelf attributes. Occluded or low-detail parts remain unknown and motivate targeted extra views.

rows.query: The grey shelf with boxes and not the empty one
rows.acceptance_focus: Audit shelf-versus-cart category alias, grey appearance, box contents and not-empty condition. Visible grey alone cannot certify the whole description.
